title: Trump Approval Drops to Historic Low of 33% as Democrats Gain Upper Hand Ahead of Midterms
snippet: With Election Day two weeks away, spiraling gas prices, economic frustration, and backlash over military action in Iran have driven President Trump's approval down to 33 percent, bolstering Democratic prospects in Congress.
content:
WASHINGTON — With just two weeks remaining before Election Day, Republicans are confronting an increasingly severe political headwind. A new Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll reveals that President Donald Trump’s approval rating has plummeted to a record low of 33 percent, offering Democrats a distinct edge in the battle for control of Capitol Hill.

According to the survey, 66 percent of U.S. adults now disapprove of Trump’s performance in office, with more than half—52 percent—expressing strong disapproval. Among likely voters, his approval sits at 38 percent. The downturn reflects widespread voter frustration with persistent inflation, rising energy costs stemming from ongoing military conflicts in Iran, and broader concerns over the administration's direction.

Midterm Outlook Deepens GOP Anxiety

The political climate represents a dramatic shift from earlier in the cycle. For the first time in over a decade, voters report greater trust in Democrats than Republicans to manage the national economy, favoring Democrats by a 40-to-33 percent margin. That shift is particularly glaring given that economic stewardship has historically been a key selling point for the GOP.

In generic congressional matchups, Democrats now hold an eight-point lead among both registered and likely voters, expanding significantly from a three-point lead recorded in July. Furthermore, 58 percent of registered voters stated they would prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress to serve as a check on Trump, compared to 39 percent who want a Republican majority to advance his legislative agenda.

Economic Strain and Foreign Policy Backlash

At the root of the administration's political struggles is a souring economic outlook. Trump's approval on the economy has dropped to 28 percent, while nearly three in four Americans disapprove of his handling of inflation and the cost of living. Nearly half of respondents—48 percent—reported being financially worse off than when Trump took office again in 2025, marking the highest level of personal financial distress recorded in Post-ABC polling in nearly four decades.

The economic squeeze is closely tied to public backlash against foreign policy decisions. A staggering 71 percent of adults now view gasoline as unaffordable following supply chain disruptions caused by military action in Iran. Sixty-five percent of Americans polled described taking military action against Iran as a mistake, while 68 percent disapproved of Trump's diplomatic handling of U.S. allies.

Turnout Disparities and District Defense

The survey highlights significant differences in voter motivation across party factions. While 75 percent of self-described MAGA Republicans indicate they are certain to cast a ballot, enthusiasm drops sharply to 57 percent among non-MAGA Republicans. Conversely, Democratic engagement remains high across both progressive and traditional wings of the party, with over 70 percent expressing certainty about voting.

Facing these headwinds, national Republican groups have begun reallocating campaign funds to shore up candidates in traditionally safe red districts—a clear signal that party leaders are preparing for potential losses in the House. Though turnout will ultimately dictate the precise balance of power come November, current polling indicates Republicans will face an uphill battle to preserve their thin congressional majorities.
